messages:
maria.g: Hey - hitting a weird retry/auth race in the Kotlin SDK on Android emulators. App calls a non-idempotent POST (file upload) and we sometimes see duplicate uploads when token refresh happens. Repro steps below.

maria.g: Repro: emulator API 29/30, okhttp 4.10, retrofit 2.9. Call flow: Retrofit -> AuthInterceptor (adds header) -> network -> 401 -> Authenticator refreshes token -> retry. Sometimes the Authenticator runs twice and triggers two uploads.

devon.t: Ugh. I've seen double-refresh when body can't be retried because request.body() is one-shot. Is your interceptor creating a new request or mutating the existing one?

maria.g: Interceptor does: request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", "Bearer $token").build() — Authenticator uses synchronous refresh and then returns request with new header. We tried enabling retryOnConnectionFailure(true) but no luck.

jeff.k: Two quick checks: (1) Are you using an Authenticator (okhttp.Authenticator) rather than an interceptor for the refresh path? (2) Are you cloning the request body for streaming uploads?

maria.g: We are using Authenticator. Code snippet:

```
class TokenAuthenticator : Authenticator {
  override fun authenticate(route: Route?, response: Response): Request? {
    val newToken = TokenStore.refresh() // blocks
    return response.request.newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $newToken")
      .build()
  }
}
```

maria.g: Sometimes TokenStore.refresh() is called twice concurrently. Looks like two failed requests race to refresh.

anna.p: This is a known tricky one: okhttp may run multiple routes or replay the request in a way that races if the refresh isn't synchronized. We had a fix in positive parity SDK where refresh is left of the dispatcher to a single mutex. Are you deduping refresh operations?

maria.g: Not currently. We rely on TokenStore to be cheap but refresh hits network. Any suggested pattern?

devon.t: Locking around refresh is common. e.g., double-checked locking so only one coroutine/future does the actual HTTP refresh; others wait and read cached token. Also ensure the request body is replayable or mark non-replayable and short-circuit retry.

jeff.k: Also watch interceptor/Authenticator ordering: if you add an application interceptor that consumes body, it might prevent retry. For file uploads we usually: 1) use a custom request-body that supports createNewStream/clone, or 2) avoid automatic retry on 401 and do explicit retry after refresh in app code.

maria.g: Patch idea: make TokenStore.refresh synchronized with a simple mutex and return cached token if another refresh just updated it. Implemented quickly and reduced dup uploads but still seeing rare dup on Pixel 5 emulator with Android 12.

devon.t: Emulators have weird connection pooling behaviors. Try setting connectionPool( ConnectionPool(0, 1, TimeUnit.SECONDS) ) temporarily to force new connections and see if it reproduces. Also check keepAlive duration differences.

maria.g: Good call. I toggled connection pool to 0 for repro and the dups went away in that run.

anna.p: That suggests a connection-reuse + race: two requests reusing same socket and both get 401, okhttp enqueues both authenticate flows. When connection reused, OkHttp may attempt a stream->newStream flow that causes both to retry at nearly same time. Workarounds: serialize refresh via TokenStore, make body replayable, or explicitly disable automatic retry on auth failure for upload endpoint.

jeff.k: For SDK parity: our Java sdk (server-side) historically used request-level dedupe of refreshes. We should add that pattern to the Android SDK. Also update docs: "non-idempotent requests should not rely on default Authenticator retry".

maria.g: Agreed. I'll prototype a singleflight / mutex refresh helper and a RequestBody wrapper that buffers small uploads to memory for replay. For large uploads we'll fail fast and surface a clear error to app: "cannot retry after auth refresh — client must re-upload".

devon.t: Can you share the small helper? We can microreview.

maria.g: POC: 
```
class SingleRefresh {
  private val mutex = Mutex()
  private var lastToken: String? = null

  suspend fun getOrRefresh(current: String, refreshFn: suspend () -> String): String {
    if (current != lastToken) return current
    mutex.withLock {
      if (current != lastToken) return lastToken ?: current
      val newTok = refreshFn()
      lastToken = newTok
      return newTok
    }
  }
}
```

maria.g: Not perfect (coroutine usage vs blocking in Authenticator) but shows idea.

jeff.k: If your Authenticator is blocking (synchronous), wrap a synchronized block around refresh and a volatile token var to minimize blocking. Keep it small.

release-bot: deploy 1768123500 started to devex-sdk: android-auth-fix (maria.g) :rocket:

maria.g: Deploy landed. After running a few hundred automated emulator runs with connectionPool on, dup uploads dropped to near-zero. Still want to add docs and a short code sample about retries and non-idempotent endpoints.

anna.p: Please open a small RFC in docs repo and add a note in the SDK migration guide: "Android: Authenticator refresh should be serialized; non-replayable bodies will not be retried automatically." Add the request-body wrapper snippet as an appendix.

maria.g: Will do. Thanks all 🙏. If anyone has a quick checkbox list for QA on different Android versions/emulators, share and I'll run it.

devon.t: Quick checklist: Pixel 5 Android 12/13, Nexus emulator API 29, low memory (~512mb) emulator, flaky network (toggle airplane mode), connection pool default vs 0, okhttp 4.9/4.10. Also test with file >5MB buffered vs streaming.

maria.g: Perfect — I'll run those and paste results here.
